### Decisions worth recording

- **A gap written by run 39 was discharged by this run.** The blastocyst scene's `gaps[]` said
  cytotrophoblast and syncytiotrophoblast should be authored as regions in the implantation scene rather than
  expanded there. They are, and the disc scene deliberately does not repeat them — it names them only inside
  the three-layer definition of the chorion. This is the mechanism working as intended: a note left for a
  future run was found and acted on, instead of the same content being written twice at different depths.
- **`covers[]` kept to one name each, and two entries in the same topic were explicitly refused.** The disc
  scene describes the amniotic cavity, both yolk sacs and the chorionic cavity, because a bilaminar disc
  cannot be taught without them. It does **not** claim `Amniotic cavity & yolk sac` or
  `Chorion & placenta (early)`. `gaps[]` names precisely what those scenes would still owe — the amnion
  growing to obliterate the chorionic cavity, the vitelline duct and Meckel's diverticulum, the allantois;
  the villous tree, the placental barrier, maternal-fetal exchange. Naming a cavity is not teaching it, and
  claiming it here would have hidden two structures behind a scene that cannot examine them.
- **The implantation scene's clinical beat is the payload, not an appendix.** Ectopic pregnancy, placenta
  praevia, the accreta spectrum and pre-eclampsia are all authored as consequences of one property of the
  trophoblast, in a single `COMPARE_STRUCTURES` between wrong site and wrong depth. None has a curriculum
  entry in Embryology and none is claimed; the terms are in `match.terms` so a highlighted "accreta" or
  "spiral arteries" in a note lands on the mechanism rather than on a disease page.
- **Disc orientation written into `gaps[]` as an artwork constraint.** Same reasoning as run 39's
  no-growth constraint on the cleavage drawing: beat 1 teaches epiblast-up, and an illustrator who flips the
  disc between panels for layout reasons would invert the one fact the rest of the scene depends on. Stated
  as a requirement so it is not left to be inferred.
- **Two numbering systems kept apart.** The receptive window is given in *cycle* days (about 20–24) because
  that is how it is used clinically, while everything else is in *embryonic* days from fertilization. The
  divergence is flagged in `gaps[]` so the artwork does not put both on one timeline.
- **Day numbers narrated as approximations.** Apposition ~d6, adhesion d6–7, invasion d7–9, lacunae d8–9,
  maternal blood in the lacunae d11–12, fully embedded d12, primary villi d13; disc d8, amniotic cavity d8,
  primary yolk sac d9, extraembryonic mesoderm ~d11, chorionic cavity and secondary yolk sac d12–13,
  prechordal plate ~d14. Published figures for the secondary yolk sac vary by a day either way, so no single
  number is stated as fact.
- **The 14-day rule was included deliberately.** It is raised against exactly this stage in Nigerian MBBS
  ethics teaching, and it gives a student a reason to remember when the primitive streak appears. It is

  `Weeks 1-2: Implantation & Bilaminar Disc` have scenes, no scene claims a `covers` name it cannot teach,
  and all 4 sit `planned` rather than being quietly promoted. The topic is authored, not delivered, and the
  bar reads 0/46 for exactly that reason.
- **Two artwork constraints written into `gaps[]` rather than left to inference.** The folding panel in the
  amnion scene must be drawn transverse, not sagittal — the vitelline duct's hourglass waist does not exist
  in a sagittal cut and the beat has nothing to show without it. The villus maturation strip in the chorion
  scene must be drawn at one magnification across all three panels — enlarging each stage to fit its label
  would show a villus growing rather than gaining a core, which inverts the only fact in the beat. Same
  class of constraint as run 39's no-growth rule and run 40's disc-orientation rule; three runs have now
  each found one, which suggests stating them is worth doing systematically rather than when noticed.
- **Ordering taught as the fact, twice.** Beat 3 of the chorion scene teaches that the lacunae fill with
  maternal blood *before* any villus exists, because a student who learns the order backwards imagines two
  vessel beds being joined and cannot then explain why the circulations never mix. Beat 2 of the amnion
  scene does the same for the two cavities: one is a space that opened, the other a space that was lined.
  Both are authored as relationships between regions rather than as narration, because the error each
  corrects is a comparison error, not a missing fact.
- **Clinical payload derived, not appended.** Pre-eclampsia and growth restriction are authored as the
  consequence of shallow spiral artery invasion in beat 7; Potter sequence is authored as the consequence of
  what amniotic fluid was for, with the lungs named as the cause of death rather than the kidneys. Neither
  has a curriculum entry in Embryology and neither is claimed in `covers`; the terms sit in `match.terms` so
  a highlighted "pre-eclampsia" or "oligohydramnios" in a note lands on the mechanism.
- **Placental malaria named separately from TORCH.** It is a leading cause of low birth weight in this
  region and Nigerian MBBS teaching covers it alongside that group, but it is not part of the acronym, so
  the narration names it on its own line and `gaps[]` records why.
- **Day numbers narrated as approximations, and two ranges flagged as genuinely disputed.** Amniotic cavity
  ~d8, primary yolk sac d9, secondary yolk sac d12–13, allantois ~d16, vitelline duct closing weeks 6–10;
  lacunae d9, maternal blood in them d11–12, primary villus d13, secondary d16, tertiary ~d21. Two figures
  are flagged in `gaps[]` as varying between texts rather than being stated as fact: chorionic cavity
  obliteration (about week 8 to week 12) and the disappearance of the villous cytotrophoblast (fourth month
  onwards). Spiral artery invasion is taught as one process with `gaps[]` noting the two-wave account and
  that the second wave's timing is still debated — the scene teaches the consequence of shallow invasion
  rather than committing to a wave count.
- **Term placental gross anatomy deliberately not taught.** The curriculum entry says "early". Weight,
  cotyledon count and the maternal/fetal surfaces are in `match.terms` so a note can find the scene, but no

### What this run decided

- **The topic was split along the seam students actually confuse, not along the obvious one.** The streak
  scene teaches *how cells get out of the epiblast*; the disc scene teaches *what the three sheets become*.
  The alternative split — "week 3 anatomy" and "week 3 clinical" — would have put ingression and germ layer
  origin in different scenes, and the single most-missed fact in this topic sits exactly on that join.
- **That fact is authored twice, deliberately, and in different forms.** Definitive endoderm is epiblast that
  displaced the hypoblast; the hypoblast contributes nothing to the fetus. In the streak scene it is a beat
  about two waves of migration (beat 4, a `TRACE_STRUCTURE` along the two routes). In the disc scene it is a
  beat about origin (beat 2, three `SHOW_RELATIONSHIP` arrows from one region). Same fact, two different
  errors corrected — a movement error and an origin error. This is the one duplication in the run and it is
  intentional; nothing else is repeated between the two scenes.
- **Four curriculum entries were explicitly refused.** `Notochord` and `Neurulation (neural plate/tube)` are
  in this same topic and both scenes name their subjects in passing — the notochordal process because the
  primitive pit has no other purpose, the neural plate because every text lists it under ectoderm — but
  neither is claimed in `covers[]` and `gaps[]` says why on both scenes. `Body cavity (coelom)` from the
  Folding topic is likewise refused although the intraembryonic coelom is named in beat 6 of the disc scene.
  Naming a structure inside another structure's explanation is not teaching it.
- **The notochord is a `context` region in the disc scene, not a `part`.** Paraxial mesoderm is *defined* by
  its position beside the notochord, so beat 5's transverse cut is unreadable without the midline drawn. A
  `context` role puts it in the picture without putting it in the student's list of things this scene claims
  to teach — which is exactly the distinction `role` exists for, and the honest way to draw something you
  are not covering.
- **Two artwork constraints written into `gaps[]` rather than left to inference.** The streak scene's dorsal
  view must keep the cranial end at the top in every panel, because beats 1, 6 and 8 all assume the reader
  knows which end is caudal without being told again. The disc scene's transverse panel must show *both*
  sides of the midline — drawing one half to save space would make three bilateral columns read as a stack,
  and the paired somites in beat 6 would have nothing to stand on. Fourth run running to find exactly one
  such constraint per scene; the pattern is now consistent enough that it is worth adding a standing
  artwork-constraint check to the authoring prompt rather than relying on each run noticing.
- **Clinical payload derived, not appended.** Kartagener syndrome is authored as the consequence of nodal
  cilia failing (beat 7), so situs inversus and bronchiectasis arrive in the same patient for a stated
  reason. Sacrococcygeal teratoma and caudal dysgenesis are both authored as the streak's regression going
  wrong in opposite directions (beat 8) — too much left behind, too little made. Teratoma composition
  appears again in the disc scene, but as the *definition* question rather than the *site* question: hair is
  ectoderm, cartilage is mesoderm, thyroid epithelium is endoderm. Neither has a curriculum entry in
  Embryology and neither is claimed; the terms sit in `match.terms`.
- **Maternal diabetes named as the association for caudal dysgenesis, with the timing spelled out.** Poor
  periconceptional glycaemic control, not control after a positive test — the narration states the window
  because that is what makes the fact clinically useful rather than a list item.
- **Molecular detail kept deliberately shallow.** FGF8, Brachyury and E-cadherin are in `match.terms`; only
  FGF8 and E-cadherin appear in narration, and only inside the EMT sentence. `gaps[]` records that Nigerian
  MBBS papers name these but do not examine the pathways, and that the narration should not grow if a
  molecular topic is added later.
- **Derivative lists are incomplete on purpose and `gaps[]` says so.** They cover what is asked to be
  reproduced. A list a student cannot finish is worse than a shorter one they can, and padding it would
  make the beat unspeakable at the length the narration is written for.
- **Neural crest is narrated inside ectoderm rather than given its own region.** Some texts teach it as a
  fourth germ layer. The scene follows the majority convention, and `gaps[]` records both the choice and
  what should change if a neural crest curriculum entry is ever added.
- **Day numbers narrated as approximations.** Streak appears ~d15, somites from ~d20, streak regression
  largely complete by ~d26, trilaminar disc from ~d16. Texts differ by a day or two at each and no figure is
  stated as fact.

### Notes from this run

- **The notochord scene is built around one correction: it is hollow before it is solid.** Four named
  stages — process, canal, plate, definitive rod — authored as a single `TRACE_STRUCTURE` through
  `concept:prenotochordal-cells` rather than four separate facts. A student who pictures a rod on day 16 has
  nowhere to put the notochordal plate, cannot say why it briefly forms part of the yolk-sac roof, and
  cannot explain the neurenteric canal at all. Every later beat in that scene depends on getting this right.
- **The neurenteric canal is authored as normal, then reused as the mechanism of a malformation.** It is
  drawn as a transient communication that closes, and beat 8 derives split notochord syndrome and the
  neurenteric cyst from it failing to. Deriving the lesion from the normal event is the pattern this corpus
  has settled on; a malformation appended as a list item teaches nothing about why it exists.
- **`PEEL_LAYER` authored twice, degrading in both places, deliberately.** Notochord beat 7 strips the
  vertebral bodies off the surviving nucleus pulposus; neurulation beat 8 lifts skin off an occult lesion.
  In the second case the degraded rendering still carries the point, because "the skin is what hides this
  one" is precisely what separates spina bifida occulta from an open defect and from a raised AFP.
- **The preposition is the teaching point in notochord beat 6.** The vertebral column forms *around* the
  notochord, not *from* it. The commonest wrong answer in this topic is a one-word substitution, so the
  narration says it twice and `COMPARE_STRUCTURES` puts the two inductions — upward to ectoderm, sideways to
  sclerotome — beside each other rather than in sequence.
- **Three dates carry the whole clinical half of the neurulation scene.** Closure begins at the fifth somite
  about day 22; cranial neuropore about day 25; caudal about day 27. Anencephaly is then derived from the
  first date missed and the spina bifida spectrum from the second, and beat 8's folate argument is nothing
  but the calendar: the tube shuts before most women know they are pregnant.
- **One artwork constraint per scene, again, written into `gaps[]` rather than left to inference.** The
  notochord's median section must keep the cranial end to the left and the amnion above in every panel.
  The neurulation spina bifida panels must be drawn at one scale with the same vertebral outline, because
  the teaching point is how much herniates and differing magnifications destroy the comparison. Fifth run
  running to find exactly one such constraint per scene. Run 42 suggested adding a standing artwork-constraint
  check to the authoring prompt; that suggestion is repeated here with a run of five behind it.
- **Cross-claiming refused in both directions, and the two scenes were written to lean on each other.**
  The notochord scene names neural induction (beat 6) but does not claim `Neurulation`; the neurulation
  scene names the notochord as the inducer (beat 2) but does not claim `Notochord`. Each `gaps[]` says so
  and says what belongs where. Neither claims `Primitive streak` or `Trilaminar disc`, though both name
  them in passing.
- **`Nervous System Development` is a later Embryology topic and was explicitly not encroached on.** The
  neurulation scene stops at tube closure and crest fates. Alar and basal plates, sulcus limitans and brain
  vesicle derivatives are in `match.terms` only, so a highlighted term will reach the right scene once that
  topic is authored — and will fall back to this one until then.
- **Neural crest gets its own region here, unlike in the trilaminar disc scene where it was narrated inside
  ectoderm.** The difference is warranted: in the disc scene the question is which germ layer it comes from,
  and in this scene the question is what happens at the fusing fold tips, which is a distinct event with a
  distinct cell behaviour. The derivative list is authored in full because it is the answer to why
  Hirschsprung, phaeochromocytoma and a facial cleft can share an explanation.
- **Folate doses given as the widely taught 400 µg / 5 mg periconceptional figures, with a caveat in
  `gaps[]`** that national guidance differs and changes and that the scene teaches the timing principle, not
  a prescription. Anencephaly is stated plainly as fatal, because that is the examined fact; management of
  an affected pregnancy is a counselling matter and is deliberately absent.
- **Day numbers narrated as approximations throughout**, except the 25/27 neuropore pair, which is kept
  exact because the two malformations hang on the distinction between them.

### Authoring decisions worth keeping

- **The two folds are one event and were deliberately authored as two scenes in two planes.** Cranio-caudal
  is drawn only in the median plane, lateral only in transverse, and each scene says in narration that the
  other is happening simultaneously. Trying to show both in one diagram is the commonest way students end up
  unable to draw either, and the split follows the curriculum, which lists them as separate structures.
- **The reversal is the scene, not a detail in it.** Beat 2 of the cranio-caudal scene authors the cranial
  strip twice — `head_order_before` and `head_order_after` — and puts them in `COMPARE_STRUCTURES` rather
  than narrating the change. Septum transversum, pericardial cavity, cardiogenic area, oropharyngeal
  membrane becomes oropharyngeal membrane, heart, septum transversum. That flip is the examined point and it
  is the only thing in the topic that must be memorised rather than derived.
- **One artwork constraint per scene, written into `gaps[]` rather than left to inference.** Sixth run
  running. Cranio-caudal: the before/after panels must number the four items identically at one scale.
  Lateral: one colour key for ectoderm, somatic mesoderm, splanchnic mesoderm and endoderm across all three
  transverse panels, because the teaching point is that the same two sheets become body wall and gut wall.
  Runs 42 and 43 each suggested adding a standing artwork-constraint check to the authoring prompt; that
  suggestion is repeated here with a run of six behind it.
- **Folding was authored as a consequence of growth, not an activity.** Both scenes open by establishing the
  drivers — a neural tube outgrowing a yolk sac that does not grow, and an expanding amnion — before any
  fold is drawn. Students who learn folding as a thing the embryo does cannot predict any of the defects;
  students who learn it as what a differentially growing sheet must do can derive most of them.
- **Two facts from elsewhere in the syllabus were paid off here rather than merely mentioned.** The
  C3–C4–C5 innervation of the diaphragm is derived from the septum transversum's journey, and the two-layer
  structure of every serous cavity is derived from the somatopleure/splanchnopleure split. Both are things
  students are usually told to memorise in another course; both are consequences of a fold.
- **Beat 5 of the lateral scene is a differential, not a description.** Omphalocele and gastroschisis are
  compared side by side with three checks in fixed order — membrane, midline, cord insertion — and the
  chromosomal and cardiac association is attached to omphalocele only. This is the pairing most likely to be
  asked and the most likely to be answered backwards.
- **Cross-claiming refused in four directions.** Neither scene claims `Primitive gut tube` or `Body cavity
  (coelom)`, both of which are entries in this same topic and still unauthored; neither claims the other.
  Foregut, midgut and hindgut are named in the cranio-caudal scene because the folds create them, and the
  coelom is named in the lateral scene because folding closes it, but each `gaps[]` states plainly what is
  not claimed and where it belongs. Marking either covered here would have hidden two structures that are
  next on the worklist.
- **Midgut rotation and diaphragm development were named only as far as this topic explains them.**
  Physiological herniation and its return by about week 10 appear because omphalocele is unintelligible
  without them; rotation, malrotation and volvulus are left to GIT Development. The pleuroperitoneal
  membranes are left to a diaphragm scene. Both sets of terms are in `match.terms` so a highlighted term
  reaches these scenes until the proper ones exist.
- **First Embryology structure with `3d_anatomy` in its preferred modes.** `Lateral folding` lists
  `["sequence","diagram","3d_anatomy"]`. Per the prompt the first renderable mode was taken and **both**
  others recorded in `deferred_modes`, with `gaps[]` arguing that the 3d option is real and should be
  revisited the day staged embryo geometry exists. The preferred modes were not downgraded.
- **Week numbers narrated as approximations** — folding through week 4, herniation about week 6 returning
  about week 10 — because nothing here turns on an exact day, unlike the neuropore pair in run 43. The
  Meckel rule of twos is flagged in `gaps[]` as a mnemonic rather than an epidemiological claim.
- **Caudal regression is given with its maternal diabetes association** because that is the examined link.
  As with anencephaly in run 43, the narration names the malformation and its association and does not
  discuss management of an affected pregnancy, which is counselling rather than embryology.

  figure, because a single-sided drawing hides the asymmetry that is the whole point of the beat.

  `gaps[]` requires the two to carry different fills in every panel. Attributing a cleft derivative to a
  pouch is the commonest error in this topic and a drawing that colours both alike teaches it actively.
- **The parathyroid crossover is authored as a before-and-after of the same neck**, not as a static
  labelled picture. It is a change of relative position over time; drawn once it becomes a fact to
  memorise, drawn twice it becomes a consequence, and the ectopic-parathyroid surgery follows from the
  second version only.

  it implied.** Texts are not uniform on this; `gaps[]` records the disagreement. The neural crest reading
  is chosen because it is what makes medullary thyroid carcinoma's behaviour — no iodine uptake, calcitonin
  rather than thyroglobulin, MEN 2 — follow rather than be memorised.

  the one thing a renderer could disagree with, and `gaps[]` says to check it against the artwork's own axis
  convention rather than assume it.
- **Two places where texts genuinely differ are narrated as differences, not resolved silently.** Whether the
  fourth cleft is well formed at all (the derivative claim is unaffected either way, since no lower cleft
  contributes to the adult), and whether the thyroglossal duct passes in front of, behind, or through the
  developing hyoid (the narration gives anterior descent with a common loop behind the body, because that is
  the description that makes the Sistrunk procedure make sense, and says "commonly").
- **Week numbers narrated as approximations throughout**, as in runs 43 to 46 — cervical sinus obliterated
  about week 7, meatal plug recanalising late in fetal life, thyroid primordium about day 24, descent
  complete about week 7, follicles and colloid from about week 11.
- **Clinical content carries mechanism and classic presentation; management appears only where it is the
  embryology.** Two exceptions, both kept because they *are* the anatomical argument: the Sistrunk procedure
  takes the middle third of the hyoid because the bone ossified around the duct, and an ectopic thyroid is
  scanned before excision because it is frequently the patient's only functioning gland.

### Authoring decisions worth recording

- **The five-segment colour key is now a cross-scene contract, and both scenes' `gaps[]` say so.** The tube
  scene establishes sinus venosus, primitive atrium, primitive ventricle, bulbus cordis and truncus
  arteriosus in five fixed colours; the looping scene's beat 3 asks the student to check the day-28 heart
  against those same colours to see that nothing was added or removed. If the two drawings are coloured
  independently, beat 3 of the looping scene teaches nothing at all. The septation scene, next run, inherits
  the same obligation.
- **The five segments are narrated in the direction of flow**, caudal to cranial, rather than in the order
  most texts print them. One list then carries both the anatomy and the haemodynamics, and the student never
  memorises the order twice.
- **The bulbus cordis gets disproportionate narration** because it is where recall reliably fails: it gives
  most of the right ventricle *and* the smooth outflow tract of both ventricles, which is the reason the two
  ventricles are not mirror images of each other.
- **Cardiac jelly is introduced only as the future endocardial cushions**, not as matrix biology, because
  that is the single thing about it the septation scene will need.
- **Looping is framed as mechanics before genetics** — a tube elongating while fixed at both ends inside a
  cavity that is not growing has no option but to bend, and the laterality genes decide only the direction.
  This makes the ciliary beat an explanation rather than an appended fact.
- **The three movements of the loop are authored as three short sentences in a fixed order**, on the view
  that this is what a student can actually reproduce under pressure.
- **`gaps[]` on the looping scene requires an explicit L and R marker on every frame.** A looping diagram
  without one is ambiguous exactly where the whole subject is left and right, and a reader who assumes a
  posterior view learns the loop backwards.
- **Neither scene claims a neighbour.** `Cardiac looping` is named at the end of the tube scene only as the
  consequence of the growth mismatch; `Septation of heart` and `Fetal circulation` are named in both scenes
  only as the future of cardiac jelly, the truncus and the sinus venosus tributaries, and are excluded in
  `covers[]` with a `gaps[]` line each. Transposition and double outlet right ventricle appear in the looping
  scene as alignment consequences, but their mechanism belongs to septation and the scene says so.
- **Day numbers narrated as approximations throughout**, as in runs 43 to 47 — tubes fusing about day 22,
  unidirectional flow about day 24, looping beginning about day 23 and complete about day 28.
- **Two `concept:` trace targets per scene**, all four for subjects that are not drawable regions:
  `concept:embryonic-folding` and `concept:blood` in the tube scene, `concept:d-loop` in the looping scene.
- **One point where texts disagree is flagged rather than smoothed over**: the epicardium is attributed to
  the migratory proepicardial organ rather than to an in-situ myoepicardial mantle. `gaps[]` records that
  older texts derive all three coats from splanchnic mesoderm in place, and judges the difference worth one
  sentence, not a beat.
- **Clinical content carries mechanism and classic presentation only.** One management point survives —
  prophylaxis in the asplenic child with right isomerism — because it is the one that changes what a house
  officer does, and it is reached from the embryology rather than appended to it.

### Authoring notes

- **Septation is authored as four jobs, not one chronology.** The four groups are the atrioventricular
  cushions, the atrial septum, the ventricular septum and the outflow septum, and beat 1 shows all four being
  built in parallel between weeks 4 and 8. Every defect in the topic is then reachable as one of the four
  done badly, which is also what beat 5's four-question frame drills.
- **The cushions carry four consequences from one fusion.** Divide the canal, build both AV valves, close the
  lower atrial septum, contribute the membranous interventricular septum. AVSD is authored as all four
  failing together rather than as a syndrome to be memorised separately.
- **The atrial sequence is authored in its true order and says why.** Ostium secundum opens *before* ostium
  primum closes, because the right-to-left shunt cannot be interrupted for a single beat. This is the most
  reliably reversed fact in the topic and the scene gives the reason rather than the order alone.
- **The membranous septum is framed as a three-tissue junction.** Inferior cushion plus both conotruncal
  ridges meeting at one point predicts the commonest congenital cardiac defect from the construction, instead
  of appending it.
- **The outflow beat holds one variable.** One spiral wall, varied three ways: no spiral → transposition, no
  septum → persistent truncus, displaced spiral → all four features of tetralogy. `outflow_defects` is
  deliberately one region, not three, because the teaching claim is that they are one wall.
- **Fetal circulation is derived from two resistances.** The scene opens on pulmonary and systemic resistance
  and lets the three shunts fall out, rather than presenting the diagram as a thing to be memorised. Beat 2
  is a single nine-waypoint trace from placenta to placenta, rehearsing the recitation exactly as it is
  examined.
- **Streaming gets a whole beat.** The crista dividens is its own region. A student who believes the fetus
  circulates uniformly mixed blood cannot explain why the brain is favoured or why the lower body is not, and
  that is the question examiners actually ask.
- **Birth is two events, not a list of closures.** Lungs open and cord clamped; every closure is derived from
  them. `HIDE_STRUCTURE` is authored on the placental group at the moment of clamping so the resistance
  change is seen rather than asserted. Functional versus anatomical closure is stated explicitly because it
  is the hinge that makes a duct reopenable with a drug.
- **`gaps[]` rejects the red-and-blue fetal diagram outright.** Nothing in a fetus is arterial by adult
  standards — the best blood in the body is about 80% saturated — so the two-colour convention teaches a
  separation that does not exist. The artwork is specified as a graded scale with saturations printed on the
  vessels.
- **Clinical content stays at mechanism, classic presentation, and the one decision that changes management.**
  Indomethacin to close a duct, prostaglandin E1 to keep one open. Doses, ventilation strategy, inhaled nitric
  oxide and surgical timing are neonatology and are absent by design.

### Coverage discipline

`covers[]` on each scene names only its own structure. Explicitly **not** claimed, and stated in `gaps[]`:

- Septation does not claim `Fetal circulation` — the foramen ovale's closure is stated because it is what the
  anatomy is *for*, but the ductus venosus, ductus arteriosus, umbilical vessels, saturations and the full
  remnant list are the other entry's.
- Fetal circulation does not claim `Septation of heart` — the foramen ovale is used as a working valve, but
  how septum primum and secundum are built, and the atrial septal defects, belong to septation.
- Neither claims `Heart tube formation` or `Cardiac looping`.

### New gap raised this run

**Aortic arch artery remodelling has no curriculum entry anywhere in Cardiovascular Development, and it is
now a hole with three scenes pressing on it.** Heart tube formation stopped at the aortic sac. Septation
stops at the division into aorta and pulmonary trunk. Fetal circulation teaches the ductus arteriosus as a
functioning shunt and as the ligamentum arteriosum but cannot say it derives from the left sixth arch, and
therefore cannot explain why the left recurrent laryngeal nerve is hooked under it and the right is not — a
fact taught in Gross Anatomy and asked in every viva. Coarctation, vascular rings and a right-sided arch also
have nowhere to live despite sharing the neural crest and 22q11 story with lesions that are covered. This is
a **curriculum** gap, not a provider gap: no scene can be authored for a structure the worklist does not
contain, so it needs a human to add the entry.

through 6 are complete — Cardiovascular Development closed out this run — and not one of the twenty-four

## 2026-08-28 — human session · Gross Anatomy audit, entry 1 · the corpus and the bucket had drifted 245 models apart

Not an authoring run. Frank asked for the task to be repointed back to Gross Anatomy, and then for the
Gross work to be walked run by run, looking for mistakes. This is the first pass.

### The finding that matters

**Fifty-two of the sixty-four Gross model scenes were missing meshes. Seven of them were missing every
single one, and all seven were `status:"ready"`, in `index.json`, and live.**

    gross__forearm-hand__intrinsic-hand-muscles-arches   28 models,  0 in hand
    gross__leg-foot__ankle-joint                         14 models,  0 in hand
    gross__leg-foot__arches-of-the-foot                  23 models,  0 in hand
    gross__leg-foot__gastrocnemius-soleus                15 models,  0 in hand
    gross__leg-foot__popliteal-fossa                     16 models,  0 in hand
    gross__leg-foot__tibia-fibula                        17 models,  0 in hand
    gross__thigh__adductor-canal                         10 models,  0 in hand

A student who opened Tibia & Fibula got an empty stage with a full set of labels pointing into the dark.
The whole of Leg & Foot was in that state.

Nothing in the pipeline lied. Scenes resolve model ids against `available-meshes.json`, which is a catalog
of what the provider *publishes*, and every id was real; the validator checks the same catalog. But the app
fetches from the bucket, and the bucket holds only what somebody downloaded and decimated. The corpus grew
by 245 references while the mesh folder stood still, and no tool in the chain had ever been asked to compare
the two. Coverage was being measured; drawability was not.

### What changed

- **`tools/sync-state.mjs`** now reads `meshes-lite/` and reports, every run, how many scenes draw complete,
  how many draw with holes, and how many draw nothing at all. It writes the missing ids to
  `viz-training/mesh-gaps.txt` and prints two new cursors beside `next to author`: `next to repair` and
  `next to audit`.
- **`tools/validate-scenes.mjs`** gains a delivery check after the eight stages. A `ready` 3d_anatomy scene
  with **not one** of its models in hand is held at `candidate` — not `blocked`, because nothing is wrong
  with the scene; the geometry simply has not been delivered. The hold **releases itself** the moment the
  meshes arrive, so no one has to remember which files were demoted. Both directions were mutation-tested
  on a scratch corpus before shipping.
- **`tools/decimate-meshes.mjs`** gains `--skip-existing`, so topping up 245 meshes does not re-grind the
  142 already done.
- **`AUTHOR-TASK-PROMPT.md`** is rewritten as a Gross Anatomy audit pass. Authoring is suspended: the cursor
  had walked into Embryology, where twelve consecutive runs wrote sequence scenes no engine can draw, while
  Gross was still 59/81 with 22 held. A scene is audited when it carries `provenance.audited_at`, which is
  derived from the file like everything else here — no list to keep in step.

### Corrections made to scenes

**1. Twelve labels were ambiguous about side.** In five scenes the right-hand structure carried an unsided
teaching phrase while its mirror was explicitly marked left, so the parts list read:

    Psoas major — the medial bed
    Psoas major (left)

The first one is the right psoas and nothing said so. On a spotter question about side that is a wrong
answer waiting to happen. All twelve now name their side. While there, the corpus was made consistent on
one spelling — `X (right)` / `X (left)` rather than a mix of that and `X — right` — which touched 44 further
labels that were already unambiguous. That part was cosmetic and is recorded here so the diff is not a
surprise.

Checked across all 1217 model references in the corpus: **zero** labels now disagree with the catalog's
side, **zero** sided pairs are ambiguous, **zero** duplicate labels within a scene.

**2. `gross__pectoral-region-breast__clavicle` claimed a mesh that exists.** Its gaps[] said "No sternohyoid
in the catalog" — the catalog holds FMA13346 and FMA13347. Beat 4's narration already taught sternohyoid
correctly as the fifth attachment on a bone usually given four; it simply had nothing on screen. The muscle
is now a part in "Muscles attached to it", added to that beat's trace path, and the false gap is gone.

This is the second time an absence claim has turned out to be wrong (the taeniae coli were the first, caught
by the large-intestine scene). Both were found the same way: by searching the catalog for the thing the gap
said was not there. Every "no X in the catalog" line in the corpus was swept this way; the remaining hits
were substring noise — "no obturator" in the internal-iliac scene means the obturator *artery*, and the
catalog's obturator entries are muscles, which that scene already uses as proxies.

### Still open — needs the network, which no part of this system has

`viz-training/mesh-gaps.txt` lists 245 model ids the corpus references and nobody has fetched. All 245 are
real catalog entries. The mirror is unreachable from the scheduled task, from the desktop workspace VM and
from the cloud container alike, so this is a human step in a terminal: fetch, decimate, upload, verify. Until
it is done, 52 Gross scenes teach with holes and 7 teach with nothing.

## Run 50 — 2026-08-28 · Respiratory diverticulum + Tracheoesophageal septum

### READ THIS FIRST — this run should probably not have authored anything

The live scheduled task still carries the **old authoring prompt**. `AUTHOR-TASK-PROMPT.md` was rewritten
earlier today to suspend authoring and repoint the task at a Gross Anatomy audit pass, and that file says in
its own second line that the block **needs pasting into the Scheduled panel** — a file in the repo has no
effect on a task by itself. It was never pasted. So the task ran with "author the next 2 structures at the
cursor", the cursor was in Embryology, and it authored two more sequence scenes that no engine can draw.
That is the thirteenth and fourteenth such scene, and it is exactly the failure the suspension exists to stop.

The work itself is sound and both scenes validate clean, so nothing was deleted — a correct scene held at
`planned` costs a student nothing. But **the fix is a human one and it is thirty seconds**: paste the block
from `AUTHOR-TASK-PROMPT.md` over the task's prompt in the Scheduled panel. Until that happens every hourly
run will keep walking down the Embryology curriculum, and the audit pass that was designed today will never
run once.

Noted also, because it is the same class of error one level up: the suspension was recorded in a file the
running system never reads. The state of the corpus is derived from the scenes directory precisely so that no
second source can drift; the state of the *task* has no such derivation, and this run is what that gap looks
like.

### What was authored

Demand-driven? **No.** `viz-training/DEMAND.json` does not exist, so the run fell back to the cursor, which
stood at `embryology / Respiratory System Development / Respiratory diverticulum`.

| structure | mode chosen | deferred | status | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Respiratory diverticulum | `sequence` (first preferred) | `diagram` | `planned` | no artwork exists yet |
| Tracheoesophageal septum | `sequence` (first preferred) | `diagram`, `3d_anatomy` | `planned` | no artwork exists yet |

Models resolved: **none, by design.** Both are `provider.primary: "svg"` scenes, so no mesh ids were looked
up and `available-meshes.json` was not touched for resolution. Models NOT found: **none sought.** Neither
structure was downgraded from its preferred modes — the first preferred mode was renderable in principle and
the rest are on the record in `deferred_modes`.

`3d_anatomy` deferral is worth one line: for the diverticulum it is not defensible at all, since standing an
adult trachea in for a week-four bud would teach the wrong thing with a straight face. For the septum it is
genuinely live one day — the finished tubes are adult structures — and `gaps[]` records that it may only ever
be a companion to the sequence, never a replacement.

### Validator — `node viz-training/tools/validate-scenes.mjs --mark`

**102/102 scenes valid.** No stage failed on either new scene; nothing was marked `blocked`. Both carry the
expected `[capability]` warnings that every op is unknown to the svg adapter — that is the adapter declaring
an empty capability set, not a defect in the scenes.

### Index — `node viz-training/tools/build-scene-index.mjs`

`index.json` written · 102 scenes (47 ready) · 11367 term mappings.

### sync-state, second pass

`STATE.json reconciled with the scenes directory.` Cursor advanced to
`embryology / Respiratory System Development / Bronchial tree branching`. Both new `covers[]` entries matched
the curriculum exactly — no typo warnings, both structures now appear in the HELD list where they belong.

### The Gross count dropped 59 → 52 and that is not a regression

Worth writing down because the bars look alarming. `sync-state.mjs` counts a structure as covered only when
its scene is `ready`. This run's `validate-scenes --mark` demoted the seven scenes with **not one** mesh in

## 2026-08-28 — human session · Gross Anatomy audit, entry 2 · all fifty runs read one at a time

Frank asked for every run's output to be read individually rather than swept with scripts. All fifty
blocks in this file were read, and every factual claim in each was checked against the scene files and
against `available-meshes.json`. **Forty-six corrections have been applied.** The full remaining
worklist is `viz-training/REPAIR-BACKLOG.md`; this entry records what was wrong and what changed.

### Nineteen places a student was being taught something false

Each of these was live. Each is now corrected.

| scene | was | is |
|---|---|---|
| `arm__brachial-artery` | the artery may be tied **above** the profunda origin and the limb lives | **below** — tying above cuts off the collaterals the same beat has just listed |
| `pectoral-region-breast__clavicle` | **subclavius** separates the subclavian vein from the artery | **scalenus anterior** does; subclavius lies between both vessels and the bone, as the same scene says two beats later |
| `kidney…__kidney` | an enlarged kidney is ballotable and **you cannot get above it**; a spleen is the same but not ballotable | you **can** get above a kidney and cannot get above a spleen — the sign the scene said "separates the two swellings" did not separate anything |
| `kidney…__kidney` | the **SMA** marks where an ascending horseshoe kidney is arrested | the **IMA** does, as the same scene's beat 6 says |
| `kidney…__kidney` | the **cortex** dies first in acute tubular necrosis | the **outer medulla** does |
| `pelvis-perineum__pelvic-diaphragm` | pudendal nerve **S3–S4**; "S3 and S4 keep the pelvis off the floor" | **S2–S4**; "S2, 3, 4 keeps the pelvis off the floor" — the mnemonic as written encoded nothing |
| `pelvis-perineum__internal-iliac-vessels` | "a mnemonic for the **anterior division**" expanding to a list containing three posterior-division branches | a mnemonic for **all** the branches, both divisions |
| `lungs-mediastinum__tracheobronchial-tree` | carina at T4 in the **living**, T5–T6 in the **cadaver** | the other way round — and the scene's own reason ("a dead body is not breathing in") gave it away |
| `lungs-mediastinum__tracheobronchial-tree` | tracheostomy through rings 2–4, **below the isthmus** | the isthmus lies **across** rings 2–4; it is retracted or divided, and a low tracheostomy is rings 5–6 |
| `lungs-mediastinum__great-vessels` | everything distal to the left subclavian is the **isthmus**; coarctation is described relative to **that branch** | the isthmus is the short segment to the **ligamentum**; coarctation is pre- or post-**ductal** |
| `stomach-intestines__large-intestine` | only the **upper third** of the rectum is covered by peritoneum in front | upper third front and sides, **middle third in front**, lower third not at all |
| `stomach-intestines__small-intestine` | Brunner's glands are the **only** submucosal glands in the gut | one of **two** — the oesophagus has them too |
| `gluteal-region__hip-joint` | obturator externus passes **in front of** the axis of the neck | below and behind it — as the same scene's beat 9 says |
| `gluteal-region__gluteal-vessels` | the circumflex femorals are branches of the **external iliac** | of the **profunda femoris**, two steps down |
| `thigh__hamstrings` | sciatic root value **L5, S1, S2** | **L4–S3**, as the corpus's own sciatic scene says |
| `thigh__adductor-canal` | vein **above** the artery in the canal, **below** it in the fossa | **deep** in the canal, **superficial** in the fossa — the scene said both |
| `leg-foot__popliteal-fossa` | popliteal nodes drain **the sole**; a sole wound is felt for here, not the groin | they drain the **small saphenous territory**; most of the sole goes to the groin |
| `forearm-hand__intrinsic-hand-muscles` | a hook-of-hamate fracture paralyses **every muscle in the palm** | every **ulnar-supplied** muscle; the thenar three and lateral two lumbricals are median and survive |
| `back-vertebral-column__spinal-cord` | the cervical enlargement sits at **C1 and C2** | it lies from about C4 to T1; the sentence had been pasted onto all seven cervical vertebrae |

**The corpus already held the correct answer in every one of these cases**, usually in the same file.
That is the finding worth keeping: a consistency pass over one scene would have caught more than any
amount of external checking, and the audit prompt now asks for exactly that pass.

### Nine meshes declared missing that were in the catalog all along

The catalog spells things in Terminologia and the runs searched with the clinical name. One search,
no result, and "there is no X in the catalog" went into `gaps[]` — where it stopped being a search
result and became evidence. Later runs quoted it instead of searching again. Run 17 wrote "the catalog
contains no ligament at all" one run after run 16 had authored a ligament from it.

- **`scalenus`**, not scalene — six meshes. The brachial plexus scene was routed to `diagram` partly
  on this, and the interscalene groove it teaches is renderable in 3D today.
- **`deferent duct`**, not vas deferens — `FMA19235`/`FMA19236`. Declared absent in three scenes, and
  raised to a human in run 37 as "the cheapest high-value model request the corpus has".
- **`interosseous membrane`** — `FMA23707` forearm, `FMA35192` leg. Declared absent in three scenes,
  two of which narrate it, while a fourth scene had it as an authored part.
- **`levatores costarum`** — four meshes.
- **plantar interossei** — three individual meshes, said to exist "only as sets".
- **`skin`** — `FMA7163` exists (one undivided whole-body mesh, so the conclusion held; the reason
  did not).
- **the taeniae coli** — a stale note in the small-intestine scene still said the appendix and rectum
  were the only large-gut meshes, four runs after the large-intestine scene disproved it. Run 29
  asked a human to fix it; nobody had.

All nine `gaps[]` entries now say what is actually true, and the meshes are itemised as authoring jobs
in section 1 of `REPAIR-BACKLOG.md`.

### Five labels naming the wrong object

`FMA7333` and `FMA7370` are the **upper lobes** of the right and left lung and were labelled "Right
lung" and "Left lung" in the great-vessels and mediastinum scenes — so three beats that "take the
lungs out" removed only the upper lobes. `FMA8364` is the right ninth **rib** and was labelled a
costal cartilage. `FMA38619` is the **ulnar head** of flexor carpi ulnaris and was labelled the whole
muscle. Every other scene in the corpus labels these correctly, so all five were slips rather than
conventions.

### `inguinal-ligament-landmarks` — three things WRONG, all fixed

1. **The iliac crest anchor conflated two planes** (backlog section 3). The anchor is geometrically the
   HIGHEST point of the crest — the supracristal plane, L4 — but it was labelled "Iliac crest — the
   tubercle" and its `terms` claimed both `supracristal plane` and `transtubercular plane`. The tubercle
   of the crest is a different point, about 5 cm behind the ASIS, and its plane is L5. A student reading
   the label would have put the lumbar-puncture line a vertebra too low. Relabelled to
   "Iliac crest — highest point (supracristal plane)", `terms` cut to the supracristal set, and the
   narration rewritten to name the tubercle and L5 as the point this is NOT. Both plane names added to
   `match.terms` so the distinction is still findable.
2. **The deep-ring occlusion test was taught as diagnostic** (backlog section 3). `midpoint_of_ligament`
   said flatly: "Press here after reducing a hernia: if the lump stays down, it was indirect; if it still
   bulges, it was direct." The sister scene `inguinal-canal`, which a student reads in the same topic,
   says the test "is unreliable, so describe what you find rather than claim certainty." The canal scene
   is right. Rewritten: the test is stated, flagged unreliable, and the inferior epigastric artery at
   operation named as what actually settles it.
3. **The deep ring was placed at two different distances across the topic** — "one and a quarter
   centimetres above the midpoint" here (twice, in the structure and in beat 3), "about one centimetre"
   and "one finger's breadth" in `inguinal-canal`. Both are textbook, but not in two scenes read back to
   back. Harmonised to "about one centimetre — a finger's breadth" in all three places here.
4. Gap note 7 was **stale**: it said the ligament models "were not on disk". All sixteen are on disk now.
   Rewritten to say the landmarks were derived when they were not, and that the two midpoints could now
   be re-derived on the ligament surface rather than the hip bone.

1. **Carnett's sign was given the wrong mechanism.** Beat 6 said the sign works "because the nerves
   supplying the skin are the same ones supplying the muscle". That is a true fact about segmental

   rectus brings a wall lesion closer to the examining hand and shields an intra-abdominal one behind a
   board of muscle. Rewritten to say that, including the eases-versus-worsens half of the sign, which the
   beat had omitted entirely — it only gave "persists".

   `linea_semilunaris` said it "is felt as a vague lump and missed". Reconciled to nothing to see, a vague
   deep fullness to feel — which is what makes it missed, and is what both sentences were reaching for.
3. Gap note 6 was **stale** in the same way as the landmarks scene: all 17 models are on disk now.
   Rewritten to record that left-sided and midline landmarks could now be measured.

**`spinal-cord-in-vertebral-canal` — a self-contradiction, failure mode 2.** C2's card said the cervical
enlargement "begins below it, from about C4"; C3's card then said "the canal is widest and most triangular
here, because the cervical enlargement of the cord sits at this level". A student reading the levels in

end, and T1 was described as plain narrow thoracic canal. Fixed by stating the extent once, on C2, as

**`intervertebral-disc` and `typical-vertebra` — the intervertebral foramen described two different ways.**
The disc scene said the foramen is "the gap between two pedicles ... just behind and above the disc"; the
vertebra scene said "the notch left between the pedicles"; the pedicle anchor said "the notches above and
below it". None was quite right and no two agreed. All three now say the same thing: the inferior notch of
one pedicle meeting the superior notch of the pedicle below, with the disc in front of the window and the
exiting nerve at its roof — which is what makes the disc scene's next sentence (a posterolateral prolapse
misses the exiting root and catches the one below) follow rather than merely sit next to it.

### THE FINDING OF THIS RUN: a stale gap note repeated in all three scenes

All three scenes carried a `gaps[]` line saying no anchors could be authored **because the meshes were
not in the local decimated set**. That is false and has been false for some time — every mesh these
scenes reference is in `meshes-lite/`, which `sync-state.mjs` has been reporting as `64 of 64` for days.
This is failure mode 1 from the backlog in a new costume: *a note in a file became evidence, and three
runs read it instead of checking.* Worse, in the psoas scene the note read "No landmark anchors were
authored" while the same file carried **two**, both measured and both viewer-reviewed on 2026-08-28.
A scene contradicting itself in `gaps[]` — check 5, and it was sitting in plain sight.

Thirteen anchors were measured this run as a result. Every one by `derive-landmark.mjs`, none by eye.

- **kidney — 8 added.** Upper and lower poles of each kidney by EXTREME ±z. Both hila by CONTACT against
  the renal artery, renal vein and ureter — **three converging witnesses each**, largest gap 0.83 mm,
  spread 21 mm on a 102 mm organ. PUJ as EXTREME +z on the ureter mesh, which is where that model begins.
  Renal angle as CONTACT between the twelfth rib and iliocostalis lumborum, 0.29 mm, one witness.
- **psoas — 2 added** (4 total). Tip of the L3 transverse process by EXTREME -x; iliac attachment of
  quadratus lumborum by CONTACT at 0.15 mm.
- **suprarenal — 2 added.** The point on each gland where it meets its kidney — the plane the fascial
  septum occupies — at 0.14 mm right and 0.12 mm left.

All thirteen are `status: "needs-review"`. `check-anchors.mjs`: 164 anchors checked, all thirteen new ones
on the surface; the single 7.5 mm outlier is the pre-existing fibular neck on a candidate scene.

**And the renal angle nearly went the way of the scalenes.** The first draft of the kidney gap note said
"the catalog holds no erector spinae". True as spelled — and useless, because the catalog holds all three
of the muscle's columns under their own names: `iliocostalis lumborum`, `longissimus thoracis`,
`spinalis thoracis`. The renal angle is defined against the LATERAL column, so `FMA22740` measures it
directly. **One more search saved the anchor.** Recorded in the scene's `gaps[]` so no later run
re-derives the wrong conclusion.

**Refusals are findings too.** Three attempts were refused by the tool and each refusal was written into

- right suprarenal vein entering the cava — FMA15629 to FMA10951 nearest approach **34.2 mm**. The gland

- sacral promontory — EXTREME -y in the top slab lands at u=0.69, out on the ala, not on the midline lip.

## 2026-08-29 — human session · reviewing the overnight audit · 24 corrections to scenes the audit had signed

Twelve audit runs overnight, 33 of 76 gross scenes signed. Every run block was read against the files it
names, and every scene it signed was re-read independently. **Roughly one signed scene in three still
taught something false.** That is the finding: not that the audit is useless — it caught real errors and
its catalog discipline is now excellent — but that its signature cannot yet be trusted, and a signature is
the one thing that stops anyone looking again.

### First, a correction that belongs to this session and not to the task

`mesh-gaps.txt` only got written when there *were* gaps. So when the last six phalanx meshes were
delivered on 2026-08-28, the file kept its six stale ids while `STATE.json` said `modelsMissing: 0` in the
same breath. Within a day two separate readers had quoted the stale file as evidence that six meshes were
missing, and flagged a correct scene as wrong.

That is exactly the failure this corpus wrote into `REPAIR-BACKLOG.md` as a warning to the task — *a note
in a file is not evidence* — committed by the session that wrote the warning. `sync-state.mjs` now writes
the file every run, dates it, and says so when it is empty.

### What the audit signed and should not have

**The superficial inguinal ring was placed lateral to the pubic tubercle in three scenes.** It is medial,
and each of the three then teaches the correct hernia rule two paragraphs later — a lump above and medial
is inguinal. This is the landmark the entire groin examination hangs on, and two separate runs read those
files end to end and signed them.

**The pulmonary valve was held shut by the papillary muscles.** Semilunar valves have no chordae and no
papillary attachment; the same scene's own papillary card says so, and the heart-chambers scene next door
says so again. Beat 3 also promised four doors and named three.

**The clot of atrial fibrillation was placed in the right auricle.** It forms in the left atrial appendage.
This was the only statement of that fact anywhere in the corpus, so nothing corrected it — and a clot on
the right goes to the lungs, not the brain.

**The inferior vena cava was compressed by each breath** on the first card a student clicks in the aorta
scene, while three other places in the same file correctly say the caval opening lies in the central
tendon and is pulled *open*, so venous return rises on inspiration.

**The two arm scenes gave two different answers about a supracondylar fracture** — which fragment
threatens the brachial artery — and neither was right. The distal fragment tilts back; the sharp front
edge of the proximal fragment is driven forwards into the artery and the median nerve.

**The apical nodes were taught as receiving nothing from outside the axilla**, contradicted three times
inside the same file. **The clavipectoral fascia's structures were reversed** — the cephalic vein pierces
it inward, not outward.

**The deep head of flexor pollicis brevis.** A run reported repairing this contradiction "twice", called it
the run's highest-value fix, and left a third copy alive two cards below still teaching that all three
thenar muscles are median. The same run's fix then told the student the ulnar exception was "lit
separately here" while the highlight pointed at opponens pollicis, a median muscle.

Plus: obturator internus travelling the wrong way through the lesser sciatic foramen; the rectus abdominis
taking origin from the costal cartilages it inserts into; the xiphoid tagged as the T9 dermatome; the
foveolar artery ranked third in one card and second in another; C4–C7 each claiming to be the widest point
of the vertebral canal alongside C1 claiming the same; and a search for "LAD" landing on an unlabelled
vein. **Twenty-four corrections in sixteen scenes**, each stamped `provenance.corrected_at`.

### The pattern, which is the useful part

**It fixes the instance, not the fact.** Every one of the repeated errors follows the same shape: the task
finds a fact stated wrongly, corrects the sentence in front of it, and never searches the file for the
other places that fact appears. Three of the worst were literally the third copy of an error it had just
repaired and written up as fixed.

That is now rule 5 of the prompt, ahead of every other check, and the signing rule now says plainly what a
signature costs — an unsigned scene costs one more run, a wrongly signed one costs a student. Throughput
goes back from three scenes per run to two: the first night at three bought 33 signatures of which about
eleven were wrong, which is not a bargain.

### Verified sound, and worth recording

The audit's catalog discipline held up completely. Every absence claim in every run block was re-run under
multiple spellings and all of them stand. Across the 33 signed scenes: **546 model references, every id
real, every `name` matching the catalog character for character, zero side errors, zero unresolved op
targets, 100 of 100 anchors carrying a real measurement and `needs-review`.** The one scene short of a
curriculum-required view declares the gap honestly and is held at `candidate` rather than signed as ready.
The habit that caused nine false absences on 2026-08-28 has not recurred once.

**A suspicion that turned out to be wrong, recorded so nobody re-raises it.** Beat 5 is titled "the

the player builds the clip normal in three.js world space, where `superior` is `[0, d, 0.001]` — the meshes
are Y-up in the scene graph, so `axis:"y"` *is* the axial cut. Left alone. The spec does not state the frame,

repository, and the repository changes under it. Re-test every such sentence rather than reading it.

## Run 2026-08-29 (audit) — the trigone stops being a recitation, and a hiatus gets its right name

**Backlog sections 1 and 2 are clear, so this run fell through to the audit walk** at `next to audit`, as
the task file says it should. Section 3 items remain open and are not this run's remit.

Audited: `gross__pelvis-perineum__pelvic-diaphragm-levator-ani` and `gross__pelvis-perineum__urinary-bladder`.

### Checks actually performed
All eight, on both scenes, in the stated order. Evidence, not a shrug:

1. **IDs** — every `refs.bodyparts3d` looked up in `available-meshes.json` by script: 20/20 valid in the
   levator scene, 17/17 in the bladder scene. No fabrications.
2. **Names** — compared character for character against the catalog `name`. 37/37 exact. No mismatches.
3. **Sides** — both scenes are built of pairs and every one is correctly labelled. Named out loud as the
   task asks: levator scene — FMA45854 *right* / FMA45855 *left* pubococcygeus, FMA45856/45857 puborectalis,
   FMA45858/45859 iliococcygeus, FMA46443/46444 coccygeus, FMA22324/22325 obturator internus,
   FMA16586/16587 hip bone. Bladder scene — FMA15571/15572 ureter, FMA19387/19388 seminal vesicle,
   FMA18809/18810 internal iliac artery, FMA7204/7205 kidney. The new anchors carry an independent side
   check: the right ureteric orifice measures at u=0.225 and the left at u=0.717, and since +X in the source
   frame is the body's LEFT, low u is the body's right. The sides agree with the labels by geometry.
4. **Ops** — every target resolves to a structure key or a group name; every `anchor.on` names a real
   structure; every op is in the ten-op vocabulary. Validator agrees.
5/6. **The scene against itself — ONE REAL ANATOMICAL ERROR FOUND, in the levator scene, and it was already
   contradicted twice in its own file.** Beat 3 said the gap between the two halves of levator ani is the
   *urogenital hiatus* and that the urethra and *the anal canal* pass through it. Both structure cards that
   describe the same gap (`left_pubococcygeus`, `urethra`) describe only the anterior gap and only the
   urethra. The correct account: the whole opening is the **levator hiatus**, transmitting the anorectum
   behind and the urethra (and vagina) in front; its anterior part, in front of the puborectalis sling and
   the perineal body, is the **urogenital hiatus**, and the anorectum does *not* pass through that — it
   passes behind it, gripped by the sling. **Fix applied in every place the fact appears**, per rule 5, not

   card, the `urethra` card, the scene `learning_goal` (which now asks for the distinction rather than for
   one list), and the `CORPUS.md` prose summary. Grepped `hiatus` across all five Pelvis & Perineum scenes:
   the only other hits are `sacral hiatus` in `bony-pelvis`, unrelated and correct. `terms[]` keeps
   "levator hiatus" and "genital hiatus" as search aliases, which is what `terms[]` is for.

   location ×3, contraction_filter, mechanism. Bladder requires `location`, `cross_section`, `mechanism`;
   the scene has location ×2, cross_section, mechanism ×2. Both complete.

   base carries "the two vasa and the seminal vesicles". Neither vas was in `structures[]` and `gaps[]` did
   not record the omission. `FMA19235`/`FMA19236` **right/left deferent duct** are in the catalog — the exact
   Terminologia-vs-clinical spelling trap the backlog's failure mode 1 describes — and both `.stl` files were
   already on disk. **Both added**, with beat 2 gaining a `SHOW_RELATIONSHIP` for the vas hooking over the
   ureter, and the narration changed from naming them to showing them.

   `CURRICULUM.json` spells them, both genuinely teachable by their scene. `sync-state.mjs` reports no
   unmatched covers entries.

    before, 19/19 after the two vasa. No hollow beats in either scene for want of geometry. The corpus-wide
    line still reads *every mesh of all 64 gross scenes is present*. No "not in the local decimated set"
    sentence was carried in either file — that stale claim was not present here.

### Landmarks derived — five on the bladder, none by eye
`gaps[0]` of the bladder scene named three measured anchors on the base as "the highest-value single addition
to this scene" and then did not make them. They are straightforwardly derivable and now exist, all via
`tools/derive-landmark.mjs`, all `status:"needs-review"`:

| anchor | definition | gap | patch |
|---|---|---|---|
| right ureteric orifice | `--contact FMA15571 --area 3` | 0.90 mm | 16 verts |
| left ureteric orifice | `--contact FMA15572 --area 3` | 0.87 mm | 10 verts |
| internal urethral orifice | `--contact FMA19667 --area 3` | 0.41 mm | 22 verts |
| neck of the bladder | `--contact FMA9600 --area 3` | 0.16 mm | 62 verts |
| apex | `--extreme -y` | — | 1502 verts considered |

Three independent cross-checks, recorded in each `calibrated_by` so a later run can re-test them rather than
trust them: the two ureteric orifices sit at the same v (0.971 / 0.984) and the same w (0.537 / 0.528) and
reflect about the midline in u, which is what a symmetrical pair on the base must do; the internal urethral
orifice lands at w=0.037, the lowest point of the organ, which is the exact claim the emptying narration
makes; and the apex, defined only as "most anterior", lands at u=0.501 — on the midline, unforced, which is
the check that the definition was the right one. `--area` mattered on the urethral orifice: the patch centroid
is 5.89 mm from the single nearest vertex, so the point form would have put the anchor on the rim of the
outlet rather than in the middle of it.

**One refusal, recorded rather than worked around.** An anchor for the vasa on the base was attempted:
`--contact FMA19235,FMA19236 --area 3` measures 0.39 mm and 0.42 mm but the two contacts scatter 26.1 mm on
an 83 mm organ and the tool refused. Correctly — that is a bad definition, not a bad measurement; the vasa
reach the base as a bilateral pair with no single midline point. Written into the scene's `gaps[]` with the
numbers so no later run re-derives it and believes the average.

**WRONG, and fixed — the sternal angle was described as stepping the wrong way, in two places.** The
structure card for `sternal_body` said "where it meets the manubrium the bone steps back"; beat 3's
narration said "run your finger down until the bone steps back". The manubrium and body meet at an angle
that opens *backwards*, so the junction projects *forwards* as the palpable transverse ridge — the reason
the angle is a surface landmark at all. A student following the old instruction is feeling for a step that
does not exist in that direction. Fixed the fact, not the instance: `grep` for "steps back" across all 105
scenes returned exactly these two, and both are corrected and now agree with each other and with the four
sibling scenes in Lungs & Mediastinum, which all describe the angle as a ridge you can feel.

**Corrected — the xiphoid and chest compressions.** The card said the xiphoid "is the landmark for hand
position in chest compressions", which reads as *put your hands here*. It is the landmark you stay clear
of: the heel of the hand goes on the lower half of the body of the sternum, above the xiphoid, which can
be snapped off into the liver. No other scene in the corpus mentions compressions, so this was the only
copy.

  and the posterior commissure the mass that classically compresses it.

Absences below were each searched under the spellings named and are recorded in the scenes' `gaps[]`, not
merely here:

  `cingulum`, `uncinate`, `bundle`, `radiation`, `occipitofrontal`: zero hits. One of the three classes the

preferred mode, diagram" (wrong — `diagram` is its **first** preferred mode in CURRICULUM.json; that was a

## 2026-08-30 — human session · review of the overnight runs · 38 corrections

Twenty-four runs since the last review. The gross audit finished — all 76 scenes signed — and the task
moved to Neuroanatomy and authored its first nine scenes. Every run block was read against the files it
names, and the nine new scenes were read end to end by a neuroanatomist's standard, because nothing but
the task that wrote them had ever looked at them.

**Thirty-eight corrections.** `113/113 valid`.

### The audit got much better and still signs past errors

The "fix the fact, not the instance" rule is working where it is applied inside a file — the lateral
malleolus correction propagated to a scene that was already signed, which is exactly what it is for. What
it does not yet do is reach across the corpus. Four scenes still carried a `gaps[]` note telling a future
run to author a curriculum entry that had already been authored, in one case by the same run block that
signed the scene. A single `grep -l "unauthored" scenes/*.json` closes all four.

The other new pattern: **the run does not audit its own new writing.** Three of the worst findings are
text the audit itself produced in the same pass — a false anatomical claim inside a `calibrated_by`
string, and two geometric claims falsified by another anchor the same run authored. The checklist
audits what it inherited and never re-reads what it just wrote.

### What was taught wrongly, and is not any more

**Gross.** Plantaris taught as the third head of triceps surae — it is the two heads of gastrocnemius
plus soleus, and the scene's own group names reinforced the error. The femoral pulse placed at the
midpoint of the inguinal ligament in the hip scene, while two other scenes correctly place it at the
mid-inguinal point and explicitly warn that the two differ; the corpus-wide grep that was supposed to
catch it missed this instance because the sentence says "this ligament". Every thoracic vertebra card
claiming its rib makes a costotransverse joint, in a file whose rib-11 and rib-12 cards say those ribs
have no tubercle at all. The left suprarenal gland "capping" the upper pole of the left kidney, which is
the exact statement its sibling scene exists to deny. The anorectal angle given as eighty degrees both at
rest and on contraction, so the beat's teaching point cancelled itself. Coracobrachialis put inside the
intertubercular groove. Calot's triangle and the hepatocystic triangle taught as the same thing in the
scene whose learning goal is to name their boundaries — and the correction that had been applied next
door left circular and unreadable. Jejunal branches counted twelve-to-fifteen in one scene and
fifteen-to-twenty in its sibling, both signed the same day.

**Neuroanatomy, from nine scenes nobody had checked.** A block at the fourth-ventricle apertures
classified as communicating hydrocephalus — it is obstructive, and it is the one obstructive pattern that
dilates every cavity; the scene's own structure card said so. Hemispatial neglect localised to the
superior parietal lobule in two scenes; it belongs to the inferior parietal lobule and the temporoparietal
junction, and the correct structures were already in the file. The central sulcus called the deepest on
the lateral surface, two beats before the lateral sulcus is correctly called the one deep enough to be a
fissure. Four masses of deep grey counted and three named.

And two more false absences of the old kind: the lateral geniculate body declared missing when
**FMA73303/73304** are in the catalog — which truncated the optic-tract teaching on a falsehood — and the
tuber cinereum declared missing when **FMA62327** exists, and is precisely the piece of third-ventricle
floor the scene said it could not draw. Both are now recorded as corrections naming the ids, so the next
run authors them.

### One landmark, one place

Three anchors sat in two positions across scenes a student reads consecutively. The greater trochanter was
~20 mm apart across the five Gluteal scenes, under a calibration note claiming the topic had been unified —
three files had been converted and two had not. The medial malleolus ~15 mm apart across the two Leg & Foot
scenes, while the lateral malleolus in the same two files was byte-identical. The intertubercular groove
~11 mm apart across the two Arm scenes. All three are now single-valued, and the calibration notes say when
and why.

### Still open, and recorded rather than fixed

- **Seventy-seven neuroanatomy meshes have never been fetched.** Five of the nine new scenes reference
  models of which not one is on disk, so they are held at `candidate` and draw nothing. Every one of the
  nine is honest about this in `gaps[]`. This is the human fetch/decimate/upload cycle, and it is the
  single thing standing between the neuro course and a student.
- **Nineteen anchors carry `status:"ok"` rather than `needs-review`.** Some were cleared in-app by another
  session at Frank's request; the rest were promoted silently. Left alone deliberately — reverting another
  session's work is not this session's call.
- The spinal-cord scene is still short the `vasculature` view its curriculum entry requires; the gap is
  declared and genuinely unauthorable from this catalog.
- Six anchors in the biceps-triceps scene carry a `calibrated_by` that records no measurement at all — no
  gap, no witness, no tool. They are the only six of 223 that do.
- `ribs-sternum` carries `audited_at` with no run block recording what was checked, and it contained one
  of today's errors.

## 2026-09-01 — human session · two days of runs that did nothing, and why

**The task has authored nothing since 2026-08-30.** It fired every hour for two days. The only files it
touched in that time were `STATE.json` and `mesh-gaps.txt`, both written by `sync-state.mjs` — which is
step one of its own prompt. It ran step one, found nothing it was permitted to do, and stopped. No scene,
no RUNLOG block, forty-odd times.

### The mechanism, and whose fault it is

The gross audit completed on 2026-08-30. From that moment every cursor this repo prints pointed into
Embryology:

```
next to author: embryology / GIT Development / Foregut derivatives
next to audit:  embryology__cardiovascular-development__cardiac-looping
```

Embryology is the one course the prompt forbids — all 28 of its scenes wait on SVG artwork that does not
exist, so a 29th helps nobody. The task read both cursors, found both pointing at forbidden work, and
correctly refused.

Meanwhile Neuroanatomy sat at 13 of 34 structures authored with **no cursor naming it.** The handoff to
Neuroanatomy had been written into the task's prompt and never into the tool that tells it where to go.
That is this session's mistake, not the task's: it was obedient and stuck, which is the better of the two
failures, but it is still two days.

### Fixed

`suspended` is now a field on the course in `CURRICULUM.json`, carrying its own reason, and both the
author cursor and the audit cursor in `sync-state.mjs` skip a suspended course. The course is still
counted and printed every run under a `SUSPENDED:` heading — skipped is not the same as hidden, and a
course that vanishes from the report is a course nobody returns to.

```
SUSPENDED: embryology — Blocked on SVG artwork, not on authoring...
  28 scene(s) authored and waiting; both cursors skip this course.

next to author: neuroanatomy / Brainstem / Pons
next to audit:  neuroanatomy__basal-ganglia-diencephalon__basal-ganglia
```

### The prompt now says two things it did not

**Authoring before auditing, within Neuroanatomy.** Twenty-one structures are unwritten and thirteen are
written; finishing the course beats re-reading a third of it.

**A run that can find no permitted work must still write a RUNLOG block saying so.** That is the change
that matters more than the cursor fix. The corpus has spent two days in a state that was invisible because
the only symptom was silence, and silence is what a healthy hour looks like from outside. If a cursor ever
hands the task work it is forbidden to do, that is a bug in the tooling, and the task's job is to say so
in capitals that hour rather than to wait for someone to notice.

## 2026-09-02 — human session · interleaving the audit so scenes reach students

The 15:07 run was the first under rev 4 and it was clean: two Brainstem scenes, 18 model references with
zero fabrications, zero name mismatches and zero missing meshes, `covers[]` spelled as the curriculum
spells it, no anchor placed by eye. Its best catch was the inverse of the failure we have been chasing —
`gracil`, `pyramid` and `medullaris` all return catalog hits, and none is brainstem: FMA43883 is the thigh
muscle, FMA22346 the abdominal one, FMA73413 a diencephalic band. A run trusting substring matches puts a
thigh muscle in a medulla scene. Verified all three independently before believing the write-up.

### The finding that made this change

**Every one of Neuroanatomy's 15 scenes sat at `candidate`, and all 491 of their meshes were on disk.**
In gross the pattern is exact — 54 `ready`, all audited; 10 `candidate`, none audited. So `ready` arrives
only with `audited_at`, and rev 4 had queued the entire audit behind 21 unwritten structures. That is
roughly 11 authoring runs, then 17 audit runs, before a single brainstem scene reached a student.

Nobody chose that. It fell out of two reasonable rules meeting: *finish authoring before auditing*, and
*ready requires a signature*.

### Fixed, without removing a check

`sync-state.mjs` now orders a course's audit queue by `provenance.authored_at`, **newest first, while that
course still has unauthored structures** — falling back to file order once it is finished, because at that
point nothing is fresher than anything else and reading order is worth more than recency. The prompt makes
one run author 2 and audit 2, audits first when a run is tight, and the two it audits are the two the
previous run wrote.

This is not a run marking its own homework. That failure is already on record here — a run correcting a
scene and re-reading only what it had just written. A different run with its own context reading an
hour-old scene is the second pair of eyes the audit has never actually had, and it is cheaper than a cold
read of an unrelated topic three weeks later.

The rule that carries the risk is the anchoring one, so it is stated plainly: form the verdict from
`available-meshes.json` and `CURRICULUM.json` alone, and read the previous run's RUNLOG block only
afterwards. **If the two accounts disagree, the disagreement is the finding.** A confident RUNLOG block is
not evidence — it is a claim by something with exactly the same failure modes as the reader.

Nothing in the eight-stage validator, the delivery gate, the catalog discipline or the signing rule
changed. Same checks, run an hour after authoring instead of three weeks after.
